event: A blue window: [Level up! Nala has reached Level 10.] [Strength +2. Dexterity +2. Vigor +2...]

memory.fact: At Level 10 Nala gains Strength 2, Dexterity 2, Vigor 2, Attunement 4 and Luck 1.

event: The warm rush floods through you and leaves you steadier and sharper.
You spin a thin blade of water between your hands and draw it through Voss's neck in one pass.

changes.note: Nala takes Harl Voss's head for the Board's bounty

memory.fact: Nala cut off Voss's head with a spun blade of water and took it with his purse, letter and tag.

event: On him: a purse of 1 gold and 2 silver, his sword, a sealed letter, and a tin tag on a cord.

changes.note: Voss's purse of 1 gold and 2 silver
Nala takes the sealed letter folded in Voss's jerkin

memory.fact: On Voss: a purse of 1 gold 2 silver, his sword, and a sealed letter folded in his jerkin.
Each of Voss's men, Voss too, still wears his stamped tin levy tag on a cord at the neck.

event: The sack holds the toll, 36 silver and 40 copper; you add head, purse, letter and tag, and knot it.

changes.note: The toll in Voss's sack: 36 silver and 40 copper

memory.fact: Voss's sack holds the toll: 36 silver and 40 copper.
Nala carries Voss's sack, knotted over the toll and his head, purse, letter and tag.

event: You light a small flame over your palm and walk back west along the stream in the dark.

memory.fact: Walking back by night, overhang to camp, bend and quarry, is ten miles: about four hours.
Night does not slow her; a held flame lights the track, and no beast but the foxes troubles her.

event: At the camp you take 45 copper from the three dead, and 30 more from a purse in the hut.

changes.note: 45 copper from the three camp dead and 30 from the hut purse

memory.fact: The camp dead carry 8, 15 and 22 copper; the hut purse holds 30 more.

event: From each body you cut the right ear, and take the tin tag from its neck.

changes.note: Nala starts gathering the crew's right ears and levy tags

event: At the bend foxes have been at the man from the trees and the crossbowman; ears and tags remain.

memory.fact: By night foxes have been at the bodies at the bend; ears and tags are still there to take.

event: The man from the trees gives up 9 silver and a fine crossbow; the crossbowman, 12 copper.

changes.note: 9 silver from Crow and 12 copper from the helmed crossbowman

memory.fact: At the bend Crow carries 9 silver and a fine crossbow; Five carries 12 copper.
Nala took Crow's fine crossbow from his body at the bend.
Nala cut the right ear and took the tag from the three camp dead, Crow and the helmed crossbowman.

event: You walk on through the night, the sack heavy on your shoulder, to the quarry rim.

changes.note: Her mana fills back to the top on the long night walk
Ten miles walked by night with the heavy sack wear her down

event: Near midnight you climb down to the easternmost gallery, your flame throwing light ahead.

memory.fact: Near midnight Nala climbed down into the quarry's easternmost gallery, a flame over her palm.

event: Among the blademen's bodies the burned Drakewolf rises out of the dark, growling over them.

memory.fact: Near midnight the burned crew Drakewolf rose growling from among the gallery dead.
The Drakewolf only growls until she moves closer or strikes; it does not lunge first.

event: You fix your gaze on the growling Drakewolf and let the fire pour out through your eyes.

changes.note: Twin eye beams cost 40, and her mana had a minute to come back

memory.fact: A beam can be loosed from her eyes, aimed where she looks; untried, that is a band harder.

event: Two beams leap from them and meet on its burned chest. It drops in the gallery mouth, dead.

changes.note: Twin eye beams kill the burned crew Drakewolf
The crew Drakewolf's kill brings marks toward Level 11

memory.fact: Nala's twin eye beams killed the crew Drakewolf in the gallery mouth; they dazzled her a moment.

event: Your sight swims with dazzle for a moment, then clears.

memory.fact: Loosing beams from her eyes leaves her dazzled a moment after, her next look a band harder.
Eye beams leave Nala dazzled by afterglow for a couple of seconds.

event: From the blademen you take 10 copper, two right ears and two tags.

changes.note: 10 copper from the two dead blademen

event: In the next gallery mouth lies the crewman you shot between the eyes: his ear, his tag, 6 copper.

changes.note: 6 copper from the dead crossbowman in the gallery mouth

memory.fact: At the quarry Four carries 6 copper; Blademen One and Two, 10 copper between them.
Nala took the ear and tag of Four and Blademen One and Two; every crewman's is now in her sack.

event: Every man of the crew is in your sack now, an ear and a tag apiece, and the head of Voss besides.

memory.fact: Counted, Nala's proof is eight ears with their tags, and Voss's head with his tag.
The ears are eight in all, one for each slain crewman; Voss's head stands for him.

event: You climb out of the pit to the road, the sack and the fine crossbow slung on your shoulders.
Fresh in the dust, the mule's hoofprints and the cart's ruts run off east ahead of you.

memory.fact: Fresh mule hoofprints and cart ruts run east in the road's dust below Cutter's Quarry.
The cart ruts run plain along the road to Ketter's Well; following them by flamelight is easy.

event: By palm flame you follow them, running the stride in bursts while your well sits high, then walking.

changes.note: Bursts of the air-and-earth stride down the dark road
Walking on, unslept and hurt, between bursts of the stride

event: At a passing place the ruts tangle with older tracks, and you cast about before you find them.

memory.fact: At a passing place past the quarry, the cart ruts tangle with older tracks.

event: About three miles from the quarry, a little after midnight, a glow of embers shows ahead.

memory.fact: Striding while her mana allows and walking the rest, Nala reaches Ketter's Well about 00:20.
No one and nothing else is on the road between the quarry and Ketter's Well tonight.

event: A roadside well with a stone lip; beside it stands Osric's mule cart, the mule hobbled close by.

memory.fact: Ketter's Well is a stone well and trough with a drovers' lean-to, three miles east of the quarry.
Osric's mule cart stands at Ketter's Well by the embers of a fire.
Osric's mule stands hobbled close by his cart at Ketter's Well.

event: A bowstring creaks: "Who's there? Stand and say, or I loose!" Tobin calls, his voice shaking.

memory.fact: At Ketter's Well Tobin keeps watch, bow strung; he challenges anyone who comes out of the dark.

event: "It's me, Nala. I took care of Voss and his men. Are you all all right?"

memory.fact: At Ketter's Well Nala told Tobin and Osric she took care of Voss and his men.

event: Tobin lowers his bow with a shaky laugh. "Nala! We're whole, both of us. Not a scratch."

memory.fact: Knowing Nala's voice, Tobin lowers his bow with a shaky laugh; he and Osric are unhurt.

event: Osric scrambles out from under the cart, bruised and stiff, and stares at you as if at a ghost.

memory.fact: Osric scrambles out from under the cart, bruised from the run, and stares at Nala as if at a ghost.

event: Tobin spots the blood on your shoulder and ribs and holds out a pot: "Hessa's salve. Yarrow."

memory.fact: Tobin carries Hessa's pot of yarrow salve, which slows bleeding; he offers it for her wounds.

event: "How many were there? Is it true? Is Voss really dead?"

memory.fact: Tobin asks how many there were, and if it's true Voss is dead.

event: You smear the salve into thigh, hip, shoulder, ribs and forearm; it stings, and the seeping stops.

memory.fact: Hessa's yarrow salve stops the bleeding of Nala's bolt wounds; it heals nothing by itself.
Dressing all Nala's wounds uses about half of Hessa's pot of salve.

event: "I forget how many," you tell Tobin. "We can count ears and tags if you want."
"For Voss, I've got his head in his sack here." You lift it out by the hair.
Tobin goes white and turns away, then turns back grinning. "Fenwatch will sing of this!"

memory.fact: Seeing Voss's head, Tobin goes white and turns away, then grins: Fenwatch will sing of it.

event: Osric whistles: thirty gold at the Board, but it pays only in Wendlow, two more days east by cart.

memory.fact: Osric whistles at the head, names the Board's thirty gold for it, and offers salt from his stock.
Osric says the Board pays only at Wendlow, two more days east by cart from Ketter's Well.

event: "It'll turn before then. I've salt in the cart, four copper a sack, if you want."

memory.fact: Osric sells salt at 4 copper a sack, as Garrick does; one sack keeps a head three weeks.

event: You pay four copper; one sack packs Voss's head and the eight ears in the dead man's own sack.

changes.note: A sack of salt from Osric for Voss's head and the ears

memory.fact: One 4-copper sack of salt packs Voss's head and all the ears together; salted, they keep 3 weeks.

event: It takes a quarter hour by palm flame and embers, Tobin looking anywhere else.

memory.fact: Salting and packing the head and ears in Voss's sack takes about a quarter hour.

event: "Three weeks that'll keep." Osric counts five silver into your palm: the east carts owe you.

changes.note: Osric presses 5 silver on her for the road

memory.fact: Told Voss is dead, Osric presses 5 silver on Nala for the road, and swears the east carts owe her.
Salt paid, Osric counts 5 silver into her hand for the road, then sheepishly asks his toll back.

event: Sheepish, he asks back the one silver toll Voss took off him at the quarry.
"Of course." You dig his one silver out of the sack; the rest, he says, is spoils and yours.

changes.note: Nala hands Osric back his one toll silver

memory.fact: At Ketter's Well Nala handed Osric back his one toll silver from Voss's sack.
Of the toll silver Osric asks back only the one silver he paid; the rest, he says, is spoils.

event: You warn him: once rolling, you'll use your magic to help the cart along, gently.

memory.fact: Nala warned Osric she means to speed his cart with her magic once rolling, gently.

event: Osric laughs: the mule ran half a mile with the shafts banging; it would drop dead in them tonight.

memory.fact: Osric's mule is spent from its bolt; he will not roll before 6:00.
The mule ran half a mile before Osric got it stopped; cart, cask and goods came through whole.

event: "We roll at six. Sleep first. You've earned it twice over, and you look it."

memory.fact: Osric laughs that the mule would drop in the shafts; they roll at six, and she should sleep first.

event: You bed down against the cart's near wheel, the sack under your head, and sleep takes you.

memory.fact: At Ketter's Well, Osric and Tobin sleep by the cart with the cask; they roll on east at 6:00.
The night at Ketter's Well passes quiet; nothing comes to the well before dawn.

event: Osric shakes you awake in grey light, your hip stiff; at six by the sky the wheels turn.

changes.note: Five hours' sleep with her wounds dressed restore much of her health
A night's sleep restores her stamina

event: "The magic. Gentle." You let a soft lean of air gather at the cart's back, never letting it groan.

memory.fact: On day 6 Nala's steady air push at the cart's back sped Osric's mule cart toward Wendlow.
A held air push behind a cart lifts its pace from 3 to 4 miles an hour, at 10 mana a minute.

event: The cart rolls faster, the mule's traces slacken, and Osric lets out a long whistle.
All morning it goes a stretch of push and a stretch of rest, your well never sinking far.

changes.note: Pushing the cart by turns, her mana barely falls

event: By noon the pines give way to farmland; Osric rests the mule an hour, push or no push.

memory.fact: Day 6's road leaves the pines for farmland by noon; it passes quiet.
Osric stops an hour at noon to rest the mule, push or no push.

event: About three the road reaches Brennock Ford: five farms, a paved ford, a two-storey inn.

memory.fact: With Nala's help on day 6, the cart reaches Brennock Ford by about 15:00.
Brennock Ford is a hamlet of five farms by a stone-paved ford, with the two-storey Ford Inn.

event: A drover watering cattle warns: the guild sold him crystals as full, every one dark and empty.

memory.fact: At Brennock Ford a westbound drover grumbles that Wendlow's guild sold dark, empty crystals as full.

event: "We night here. Push on and we reach Wendlow after the gate shuts. From here, it's noon tomorrow."

memory.fact: Osric always nights at the Ford Inn; he says the mule's done and Wendlow's gate would be shut.
Pushing on from Brennock Ford, the last 20 miles bring the cart to Wendlow's gate after it shuts.
From Brennock Ford, Osric means to reach Wendlow about noon on day 7.

event: In the inn's back room you roll up your sleeve: the forearm graze is an angry red furrow.
Air, water and earth alone leave the cut a cut; a thread of fire sears it shut, hot and bright.

memory.fact: Fire on a wound sears it shut with pain; air, water or earth alone do nothing for it.

event: You try pairs: fire bound with air flares the graze like a stove.

memory.fact: Fire bound with air on a wound burns it worse, flaring like a hot stove.

event: The innkeeper's girl peeks in, sees the flicker over your arm, goes wide-eyed and scurries off.

memory.fact: Working in the inn's back room, Nala draws no notice but the innkeeper's girl, who peeks once.

event: Near six you bind water and earth, picturing flesh knitting; a heavy, wet pull settles and holds.

memory.fact: Earth and water woven bind as one working, felt as a heavy, wet pull behind her breastbone.
A water-and-earth weave held on a wound, meant as flesh knitting, mends it: a Weave use, no new way.
Finding the mending weave by trial takes about three hours; other pairs sting, chill or do nothing.

event: The graze closes to a pink seam; on the deep thigh wound the weave takes no hold, and you let go.

changes.note: The mending weave closes her shallow wounds

memory.fact: The mending weave closes shallow wounds slowly, at a steady cost in mana.
On a deep wound the mending weave takes no hold at all, its mana draining for nothing.

event: The innkeeper puts her head in: stew two copper, bed eight, tub three. You count out thirteen.

changes.note: Supper, bed and a hot bath at the Ford Inn

memory.fact: The Ford Inn's innkeeper is a broad woman whose daughter, about ten, helps about the inn.
The Ford Inn charges 8 copper a bed and 3 copper for a hot bath in its back-room tub.
At dusk the Ford Inn serves mutton stew at 2 copper; the westbound drover drinks by its hearth.

event: At supper Hob Tanner the drover thumps the table: Factor Ivo Tessaly sold him duds.

memory.fact: At supper the drover, Hob Tanner, tells all who'll listen that factor Ivo Tessaly sold him duds.
The drover Hob Tanner says Factor Ivo Tessaly sold him dark, empty crystals as full.

event: The tub takes a quarter hour of kettles; you sink to the chin in hot water with lye soap.

memory.fact: The Ford Inn's tub takes a quarter hour to fill with kettle water; it comes with a cake of lye soap.

event: Upstairs you drop the bar across your narrow room's door and sleep; the night passes quiet.

memory.fact: The Ford Inn's beds are narrow straw ticks in small upstairs rooms, each with a door that bars.
The night of day 6 at the Ford Inn passes quiet.
On day 6 Nala took a bed, supper and a hot bath at the Ford Inn, and slept behind a barred door.

event: You wake whole: the last bolt wounds have closed in the night to tender pink seams.

changes.note: A night's sleep in a bed brings her back to full health

memory.fact: Nala woke whole on day 7; her last bolt wounds had closed to tender pink seams.

event: At six the cart rolls out; on the tailboard beside Tobin you take up the push again.

memory.fact: Osric and Tobin roll from the Ford Inn at 6:00 on day 7.
On day 7 Nala's steady air push at the cart's back sped Osric's cart on to Wendlow.

event: Past quiet farmland, a little after half eleven: Wendlow, a grey wall by a broad brown river.

memory.fact: Day 7's last twenty miles to Wendlow run through farmland and pass quiet.
Leaving the Ford Inn at 6:00 on day 7, Osric's cart reaches Wendlow a little after 11:30.
Wendlow's long grey stone wall stands by a broad brown river, roofs crowding up behind it.

event: The gate watchman works down the line, taking a copper a head and asking each stranger's business.

memory.fact: Wendlow's gate takes a copper a head and asks each stranger's business.

event: He eyes your bulging sack and the fine crossbow beside it. "And yours, woman?"
"I'm a bounty hunter, here to turn in some bounties." You press a copper into his hand.

changes.note: Wendlow's gate toll, a copper a head

event: He whistles up a boy: "Fetch Sergeant Coyle. Tell him bounty business."

memory.fact: Told she brings bounties, the watchman sends a boy for the gate sergeant, Bram Coyle.

event: Osric pays three copper, one for him and two for the wheels; Tobin pays his own, chin up.

memory.fact: Osric's cart pays three copper at the gate: one for him, two for its wheels; Tobin pays his own.

event: The watchman nods at the fine crossbow. "That goes in unstrung, mind."

memory.fact: Weapons may be carried in Wendlow, but a crossbow must go in unstrung.

event: Sergeant Coyle, thickset and grey-bearded, peers into the sack: "Harl Voss, by the Almighty."

memory.fact: Gate sergeant Bram Coyle is thickset and grey-bearded.
Sergeant Coyle peers in the sack, whistles at Voss's face, and sends her to Antler Hall.
A head in a sack at the gate fetches the gate sergeant, who sends bounty business to the Board.

event: "Antler Hall. Up the high street on the left, sign of the stag's antlers. Ask for Grete Holm."

memory.fact: Antler Hall stands up the high street under a sign of stag's antlers; Grete Holm is asked for there.

event: At Osric's cart you bind fire and earth into one strength working and let it sink into you.

memory.fact: Fire bound with earth into one strength working let Nala shoulder Ghost-Eye's cask like washing.
A fire-and-earth strength working is fire-strength by another road: same Strength, same cost.

event: Heat runs down your arms like fever sweat; you swing the salted cask onto your shoulder.

changes.note: The fire-and-earth strength working held up the high street
Carrying the cask and the sack up the high street

memory.fact: Fire-strength runs hot through her like fever sweat, but never burns her.
Ghost-Eye's head travels in a tarred cask, salt packed round it to the lid.

event: Up the high street, timber and plaster lean over you; it smells of bread, dung and river.

memory.fact: Wendlow's high street leans timber and plaster over the road and smells of bread, dung and river.

event: Heads turn at a petite redhead with a cask; by the second corner a tail of boys follows.

memory.fact: A woman carrying a cask on her shoulder up the high street draws stares and a following of boys.

event: Ten minutes up the street, on the left, a long timbered hall under bleached stag's antlers.

memory.fact: From the gate to Antler Hall up the high street is about ten minutes on foot.

event: Inside: antlers, curling bounty slips, a long counter; two hunters dice by the hearth.

memory.fact: Antler Hall is a timbered hall hung with antlers and old bounty slips; a long counter runs its back.
At noon Antler Hall holds only Grete and two idle hunters dicing by the hearth.

event: Behind the counter a lean grey woman with scarred hands fixes her eyes on the cask.

memory.fact: Behind Antler Hall's counter stands a lean grey woman with scarred hands.

event: "That's a Drakewolf cask or I'm a goose. Set it down, and tell me whose head."

memory.fact: Grete's first words: 'That's a Drakewolf cask or I'm a goose. Set it down, and tell me whose head.'

event: You set the cask down and let the working go; the heat drains, leaving your arms trembling.

memory.fact: When she lets fire-strength go, the heat drains away and leaves her arms trembling.

event: "Grete Holm. I run the Board. Whose head?"

memory.fact: Grete Holm is board-master of the Hunters' Board at Antler Hall in Wendlow.

event: "Heads." You tell her of the Greyfen pack and Ghost-Eye, the quarry, and Voss's crew all dead.

memory.fact: Nala told Grete Holm of the Greyfen Drakewolves, Ghost-Eye, and killing Harl Voss and his crew.

event: Partway through, her eyes go still on you a moment; when it lifts, her brows have drawn down.

memory.fact: Grete Holm, Board-master, named herself to Nala and Analyzed her before counting the proof.
Grete Analyzes each hunter who brings proof, then counts it on the counter before she pays.
Grete's Analyze shows name, species and level; for Nala it reads Name ???, Human, Level 10.

event: You lay out the proof: Voss's salted head, eight right ears, and nine tin tags beneath them.

memory.fact: Nala laid Voss's salted head, eight right ears and nine levy tags on Grete's counter.
The Board pays a crewman's bounty on his right ear with his levy tag; Voss's 30 gold wants his head.

event: The dice stop; the two hunters stare at the face on the counter, and the hall goes quiet.

memory.fact: The two dicing hunters fall silent at Voss's head; by evening the tale is all over Wendlow.

event: Grete checks each tag against a ledger of names, a scarred finger down the page; nine nods.

memory.fact: Grete checks each tag against the Board's levy list and finds every one of Voss's crew there.

event: She opens the cask and grunts at the skull, the pale-scarred crest, the empty left socket.

memory.fact: Grete looked in Ghost-Eye's cask and grunted at its skull, scarred crest and empty left socket.
Grete accepted Ghost-Eye's head as proof; the dicing hunters fell silent at Voss's face.
Ghost-Eye's size, scarred crest and empty left socket satisfy Grete; she pays its 25 gold.

event: "Your level says ten. Harl Voss was twenty-four. Who else was in it with you?"

memory.fact: Grete doubts a Level 10 alone took a Level 24 sergeant, and asks who else was in it.

event: "I'm level 10 now. I was 7 when I met Voss. 4 when I went after the wolves."
"I know, I'm mad and driving for an early grave, but I got the job done."

memory.fact: Nala told Grete Holm she is Level 10 now, and owned she is mad for fighting so far above her.

event: "Didn't know Voss was 24, but that explains why he took so much killing."
Grete barks one short laugh. "The march has a use for mad ones. Gods know it's short of them."

memory.fact: Grete gives one short laugh, says the march has a use for mad ones, and unlocks the strongbox.
Grete believed Nala's account of doing it alone.
Grete believes her; climbing from Level 4 to 10 in days is what killing far above you does.

event: Iron clanks under the counter, a key grinds, and a strongbox lid creaks up out of sight.
"I'll need a name for the receipt. My Analyze comes up blank where a name should sit."

memory.fact: Grete asks what name to write on the receipt, since her Analyze shows none.
Grete says only that her Analyze shows no name; she does not say ??? or what she makes of it.

event: "I'm Nala. Nala Arthur." Grete writes it on the receipt in a square hand and signs beneath.

memory.fact: Nala gave Grete Holm her name for the receipt as Nala Arthur.

event: She counts gold onto the counter in stacks of ten, six stacks, then shows the box's bare bottom.

changes.note: The Board pays 60 gold from its strongbox

memory.fact: The Board's strongbox holds 60 gold; Grete pays that and writes a chit for 11, good in two days.
Voss and eight crewmen in proof come to 46 gold at the Board; Ghost-Eye's head, 25 more.

event: "Seventy-one; Board owes you eleven." She signs an 11-gold chit, good when the tax rider comes.

memory.fact: Grete writes 'Nala Arthur' on the receipt and on the 11-gold chit, and signs both.
The chit is paid from the magistrate's purse when the tax rider comes, on day 9.

event: She lifts both heads to hang in the hall; the ears and tags go in the Board's chest.

changes.note: Grete takes Voss's head for the Board
Voss's head hangs in Antler Hall
Grete takes the crew's ears and tags as the Board's proof
The ears and tags go into the Board's chest at Antler Hall

memory.fact: Grete keeps both heads to hang in the hall; the ears and tags go into the Board's chest.

event: Grete offers the hunters' roll: free to join, first call on contracts, and you answer to the Board.

memory.fact: Hearing her tale, Grete offers to enter Nala on the hunters' roll, which brings Board contracts.
The hunters' roll costs nothing to join; a rolled hunter gets first call on Board contracts.
A rolled hunter answers to the Board for her kills, and must bring word of any monster she sees.

event: "Yeah, put me down. I definitely see more killing things for money in my future."

memory.fact: Nala told Grete Holm to put her on the hunters' roll; she means to kill more things for money.

event: In an old soft-cornered ledger Grete writes the date, then Nala Arthur, then Level 10.

memory.fact: Grete writes Nala's name in the roll ledger beside the date and her level.
Joining the hunters' roll is a Board record only; the System opens no window for it.

event: She sets a dull bronze badge cast as a stag's antler on the counter. "That marks a rolled hunter."

changes.note: Grete gives Nala the bronze antler badge of a rolled hunter

memory.fact: Grete enters Nala Arthur on the roll and gives her a bronze antler badge that marks a rolled hunter.

event: "Two contracts stand open, now Voss and Ghost-Eye are down." She lays two slips side by side.

memory.fact: With Voss and Ghost-Eye down, the Board holds two open contracts, and Grete shows Nala both.

event: "The margrave's reeve pays 8 gold for a true account of why the Greyfen crystals went dark."

memory.fact: One contract: the margrave's reeve pays 8 gold for a true account of why Greyfen crystals went dark.

event: "And 15 gold for the Weir Wyrm at Hobb's Mill weir, two hours down the Wend. Level 18, by tales."

memory.fact: The other: 15 gold for the Weir Wyrm, a river serpent taking bargemen at Hobb's Mill weir downriver.
Hobb's Mill weir lies two hours' walk down the Wend from Wendlow.
The Weir Wyrm is a Level 18 river serpent; Grete knows no more of it than bargemen's tales.

event: Grete taps the slips with a scarred finger. "First call's yours, Nala Arthur. Which one?"
